## Highlights

### `ak files`: a file manager for the device and this computer

The device and a computer folder side by side in the terminal. Select with Space, press `5` to copy to the other side, or copy, cut and paste through a clipboard that stays while you change folders. Rename, make folders, delete, and see the device's recent files with `2`.

![ak files pulling photos to the computer and pasting a file into a device folder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luminousvault/homebrew-adb-extensions/v2.4.0/demo/files.gif)

- Nothing is overwritten without asking, and an overwrite keeps the old file until the new copy is complete and checked
- One progress bar for the whole job; Esc cancels and removes only what it copied
- Number keys like mc's F keys; `?` lists every key

### `ak push`: copy files to the device

Into `/sdcard/Download`, or another folder with `-d`, on one device or every one with `-a`. A name already there gets ` (1)` instead of being overwritten.

![ak push copying two files to two devices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luminousvault/homebrew-adb-extensions/v2.4.0/demo/push.gif)

### Also new

- `record` has no time limit by default: it records until Ctrl+C
- AI coding agents (Claude Code and others) get an ak skill on first run, so they use ak instead of raw adb. `AK_NO_SKILL=1` turns it off

### Changed behavior

- `pull` no longer overwrites a file in the destination: it saves the new one as ` (1)`
